content.title: About
content.content: An egg burrito is a soft wheat or whole‑grain tortilla wrapped around a filling whose core is scrambled or folded eggs, often combined with cheese, vegetables, meat or beans. The dish is popular in Mexican and American cuisines as a quick breakfast or light lunch.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg burritos are commonly served with salsa, guacamole or sour cream for extra flavor.
A “breakfast” version may include bacon, sausage or ham, while a vegetarian version relies solely on veggies and beans.
Traditional Mexican tortillas are made from corn flour, but in the U.S. flour tortillas are more common.
The burrito is portable: it can be wrapped in foil and reheated in a microwave.
There is a world record for the largest burrito – over 2 meters long.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs provide a complete source of protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs supply B12, riboflavin and folate, which support energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: When avocado or olive oil is added, the burrito delivers monounsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein, fat and fiber from vegetables helps keep you full longer.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Eggs and added ingredients (cheese, beans) contribute iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for bones and immunity.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor yolk intake.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked eggs can harbor Salmonella; ensure eggs are cooked through.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Burritos loaded with cheese, meat and sauces can be calorie‑rich, so watch portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the burrito in a microwave or on a skillet, cutting it in half. Serve with salsa, guacamole, sour cream or fresh herbs. A squeeze of lime adds a bright tang.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burrito in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
